entries.subject: physics
entries.topic: C.3-C.5 wave phenomena, standing waves, and Doppler effect
entries.unaided_evidence: Correctly identified basic reflection, interference, standing-wave formation, nodes and antinodes, and the approaching-source Doppler effect; initially confused diffraction with splitting, refraction with reflection, the resonance condition, and moving-source versus moving-observer effects.
misconceptions: Diffraction was initially described as a wave splitting rather than spreading.
Refraction changes and bending directions were initially confused with reflection.
Moving-source wavelength compression was initially conflated with moving-observer encounter rate.
entries.correction_evidence: Explained that refraction keeps frequency constant while speed and wavelength change; applied diffraction to narrow and wide openings; derived standing-wave spacing and stated the resonance condition; distinguished source compression of wavefronts from an observer encountering unchanged wavefront spacing more frequently.
entries.next_action: Complete a five-minute closed-book comparison of reflection versus refraction and moving source versus moving observer.
entries.source_basis: Learner teach-back checked against provisional general IB Physics knowledge; no official syllabus or mark scheme was supplied.

entries.subject: english
entries.topic: Paper 2 analytical chains in Stories of Your Life and Others
entries.unaided_evidence: Explained nonlinear chronology as challenging free will based on an unknown future; identified that Renee's mathematical identity makes the proof emotionally devastating; identified that documentary form makes readers form judgements.
misconceptions: Initially named broad outcomes rather than precise formal choices.
Initially described Chiang's agency as a loss rather than a redefinition.
Initially framed calliagnosia as a middle-ground or peaceful-debate issue rather than a tension between equality and coercion.
entries.correction_evidence: Produced analytical chains for nonlinear chronology, mathematical paradox, and documentary collage, linking each to reader effect and an ethical or philosophical question.
entries.next_action: On 2026-09-10, recreate three closed-book choice-to-effect-to-idea chains for Story of Your Life, Division by Zero, and Liking What You See.
entries.source_basis: Learner-provided cheat sheet and guided Paper 2 analysis practice; provisional general literary-analysis feedback.

entries.subject: english
entries.topic: Paper 2 analytical chains in Jane Eyre
entries.unaided_evidence: Explained that direct address and active first-person grammar give Jane control in the marriage ending; identified a pattern of confinement across the Red Room, Lowood, and attic.
misconceptions: Initially treated Gothic withholding mainly as shock value rather than an ethical test of trust and authority.
Initially attributed all confinement to one powerful man rather than recognising family, school, and marriage as connected institutions.
Initially needed support to name precise authorial choices before explaining their implications.
entries.correction_evidence: Produced analytical chains for direct address and active syntax, Gothic withholding, and recurring enclosed settings, linking each to agency, ethical judgement, and systemic patriarchal power.
entries.next_action: On 2026-09-10, recreate three closed-book choice-to-effect-to-idea chains for the Jane Eyre marriage ending, Rochester secret, and confined settings.
